# RG09 `tautological-assertion`: The assertion cannot fail

<!-- Generated by `realism-gate explain --markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Severity:** error (error)

An assertion compares two constants, compares an expression with itself, or asserts a literal `true`.

## Why it matters

`assertEq(profit, 100e18)` where `profit = 100e18` two lines earlier is a check of the test's own arithmetic. It passes regardless of what the protocol did, so it lends the PoC a credibility it has not earned.

## How to fix it

Assert on state read from the system after the attack, not on values the test wrote itself.

## Fires on

```solidity
uint256 stolen = 100e18;
assertEq(stolen, 100e18);
```

## Does not fire on

```solidity
assertEq(token.balanceOf(attacker) - before, 100e18);
```

## Known false-positive modes

- A deliberate sanity check of a test constant. Keep it if you want it, but it is not evidence; an `allow` comment documents that.

## Silencing it

Add a comment on the line, or the line above, with a reason:

```solidity
// realism-gate: allow(RG09) <why this is not a defect here>
```

A comment without a reason is ignored, and the output says so.
